papers.title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't

summary.tldr: A contrastive study analyzes LLM agent skills to reveal they primarily act as procedural execution anchors rather than knowledge injectors, while identifying retrieval bottlenecks and failure modes.
key_points: Skills function predominantly through procedural anchoring (65.7% of cases) to stabilize execution, compared to explicit knowledge injection (4.5%), outperforming Workflow Memory by 6.06 points in matched comparisons.
Skill retrieval scales poorly: actual-use precision drops from 29.6% to 3.3% as skill pool size increases from 5 to 100.

Exact ground-truth skill invocation is neither necessary nor sufficient for downstream task success, as downstream execution remains stable despite confusable distractors impairing offline identification.
Taxonomy development based on 8,135 normalized trial records and 238 valid open-coded labels identified three high-level categories and twelve skill-use modes.
Skills fail primarily due to brittle assumptions, incompatible contexts, or insufficient agent adaptation.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding that skills act as procedural anchors rather than fact injectors guides the design of better retrieval mechanisms and more robust self-evolving LLM agents.

papers.title: Zetta ζ: An Efficient Closed-Loop Embodied Harness for Self-Evolving Physical Intelligence

summary.tldr: Zetta is a closed-loop embodied harness that evolves code-based runtime critics and recovery skills online over three timescale-separated loops while keeping the base policy frozen.
key_points: Operates across three timescale-separated loops: action-frequency governance, rollout-level critic-recovery proposal, and validation-gated skill updates.
Utilizes Z-Infra, a rollout infrastructure that decouples agent logic from heterogeneous execution hardware.
Achieves 90.8% success on LIBERO-Pro and 93.6% on RoboCasa under fixed rollout budgets with an 11.1x inference speedup.
Enables zero-shot transfer of learned skills and demonstrates continuous scaling through self-exploration experience without updating the base policy.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes an efficient scaling path for reliable physical intelligence by enabling real-time execution governance and self-evolving recovery skills without expensive policy retraining.

papers.title: Co-RL: Unsupervised Reasoning Emerges from Diverse Cohort in Multi-agent RL

summary.tldr: Co-RL enables unsupervised reasoning in LLMs and VLMs through multi-agent reinforcement learning using peer-derived rewards from a diverse model cohort.
key_points: Trains multiple decoupled, parameter-independent models simultaneously using rewards generated by peer models instead of ground-truth labels.
Leverages cohort diversity across heterogeneous model families, varying model sizes, and rephrased training samples to prevent correlated errors and training collapse.
Achieves 3.0-8.6% average performance gains across seven text-only benchmarks for LLMs.
Delivers 2.3-7.2% average improvements across four multimodal benchmarks for VLMs, matching or exceeding supervised methods.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the reliance on costly, hard-to-scale ground-truth reward annotations for training advanced reasoning models across text and multimodal domains.

papers.title: SemComp-Bench: Benchmarking Semantic Task Completion in Video Generation

summary.tldr: SemComp-Bench introduces an outcome-oriented benchmark and VLM-based evaluation protocol for video generation, focusing on semantic task completion and grounding rather than intermediate steps or appearance consistency.
key_points: Formulates Semantic Task Completion Video Generation, evaluating models based on outcome achievement and task-relevant high-level semantic grounding against a reference image.
Constructs SemComp-Data across six domains using a scalable four-stage curation pipeline, providing reference images, detailed/brief instructions, and outcome-centric video clips.
Establishes SemComp-Bench, an evaluation protocol utilizing a vision-language model to answer structured binary questions to compute Outcome Achievement (OA) and Generation Reliability (GR) scores.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts video generation evaluation from strict appearance consistency and full sequence tracking toward functional, goal-oriented task completion.

papers.title: SemaPLC: A Project-Grounded, Verification-Gated Agent Harness for PLC Code Generation

summary.tldr: SemaPLC is an open-source, verification-gated agent harness for PLC code generation that enforces task completion using external compilation, specification, and live runtime trace execution checks.
key_points: Replaces self-judgment of LLMs with a strict completion rule gated by external specification, compilation, and live PLC runtime trace verification.
Achieved a 72.6% mean strict verified pass rate across seven models on 117 independent Program Organization Unit (POU) tasks.
Outperformed baselines on a 65-task project-context benchmark across integrated compilation, static behavior, and dynamic runtime behavior.
Demonstrated significant dynamic behavior performance gains on live PLCs, scoring 52.2 compared to baseline scores ranging from 22.4 to 31.4.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes live runtime execution and trace comparison, rather than static analysis, as the necessary standard for validating generated industrial control logic.

papers.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments

summary.tldr: SPADE is a self-play RL framework where a single LLM acts as an Environment Designer generating executable OpenAI Gym-style environments and a Reasoning Agent that learns to solve them.
key_points: Environment Designer synthesizes stateful, long-horizon environments as code featuring reset() and step() interfaces, state transitions, reward functions, and verification logic.
The designer uses the gap between the agent's reward with and without privileged hints (regret estimation) to generate tasks at the frontier of the agent's capabilities.
Critical design components include grounding the Environment Designer on pretraining corpus documents and maintaining an accumulated environment memory.
At a 30B parameter scale, SPADE yields a +5.3 average gain across eight math, science, code, and reasoning benchmarks over fixed-environment baselines.
In multi-step tool-use benchmarks, SPADE improves performance by +5.7 on BFCL-v4 multi-turn and +13.9 on ACEBench-Agent.
summary.why_it_matters: Making the environment generator a learnable component solves the goal-stagnation problem in RL, enabling open-ended self-improvement for autonomous language agents.

papers.title: EDITBRIDGE: Towards Faithful and Efficient Ultra-High-Resolution Image Editing

summary.tldr: EditBridge enables faithful ultra-high-resolution (up to 4K) image editing by framing refinement as structured data-to-data translation conditioned on the original high-resolution source using block-wise sparse attention.
key_points: Formulates refinement as a data-to-data diffusion bridge from low-resolution edits to high-resolution outputs, avoiding noise-based regeneration.
Uses original high-resolution source conditioning to prevent information divergence and texture degradation artifacts.
Introduces prior-guided block-wise sparse attention to constrain cross-image interactions to spatially aligned regions based on first-stage semantic correspondence.
Achieves 3.6x to 8.4x speedups at 2K resolution and completes 4K image editing in 61 seconds.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the quadratic memory constraints of high-resolution diffusion models, enabling fast, artifact-free 4K image editing in professional workflows.

papers.title: DiSCO: Defending text-to-image generation through distribution-guided contrastive prompt optimization

summary.tldr: DiSCO is a zero-shot, black-box defense that uses distribution-guided suffix expansion and contrastive scoring to optimize prompts, preventing NSFW content generation without modifying model weights.
key_points: Addresses the benign adversarial problem where linguistically safe prompts trigger unsafe image generation due to learned data distributions.
Uses beam search to perform distribution-guided suffix expansion at the prompt level as a plug-and-play module.
Optimizes prompts via contrastive scoring evaluated on safe versus unsafe image pools generated directly by the target model, using iterative adaptive feedback.
Requires no model retraining, fine-tuning, text encoder optimization, or access to internal model parameters.
Reduces Attack Success Rate (ASR) on the I2P benchmark by 37.7% on undefended models and 25.13% on defended models under red-teaming attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides an architecture-agnostic, zero-shot safety defense that can be deployed directly in front of proprietary, black-box text-to-image models without altering their underlying code or weights.

papers.title: LEGO-RL: Harness-Native Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents

summary.tldr: LEGO-RL bridges long-running native coding-agent harnesses with policy-gradient training using in-process LLM proxying and isolated sandbox orchestration without modifying internal harness control flows.
key_points: Uses in-process LLM proxying to capture raw generation streams for token-level alignment and log-probability recomputation, preventing train-inference discrepancies from harness compaction or re-serialization.
Employs scalable sandbox orchestration with image caching and stage-wise defenses to prevent environmental crashes and reward hacking.
Provides observable training via automated validation plugins and a Live UI for granular trajectory diagnostics.

Demonstrates performance gains on SWE-bench Verified using Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with GSPO across OpenHands SDK (64.0% to 70.4%), Claude Code (62.4% to 68.2%), and OpenCode (57.2% to 66.6%) while maintaining a rollout-training probability correlation above 0.99.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables reliable, scalable reinforcement learning for LLM coding agents directly within off-the-shelf agent execution harnesses without corrupting training signals.

papers.title: Training Leaves Traces: Centered Residual Signatures for Language Model Lineage Verification

summary.tldr: A data-free, white-box lineage verification method uses centered residual signatures from weight matrices to accurately identify open-weight language model ancestry across multiple model families.
key_points: Identifies model lineage by removing the shared identity-aligned component inherent to residual training and comparing checkpoint-specific structure across residual blocks.
Achieves an AUROC of 1.0 on residual-MLP and GPT-2 benchmarks, separating fine-tuned, LoRA-merged, pruned, and quantized variants from distilled or independent models.
Demonstrates robustness against function-preserving checkpoint laundering experiments while running 76x faster than the nearest robust baseline on GPT-2.
Validates broad applicability across six language-model families, including a case study correctly categorizing 10 public LLaMA-2 checkpoints.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables passive, fast, and reliable auditability of open-weight LLMs to verify model provenance and detect unauthorized re-skinning or laundering without requiring dataset access.

papers.title: Training Chemical Plausibility-Aware Large Language Models for Single-Step Retrosynthesis

summary.tldr: Researchers trained C3LM using Top-K prompting on a 45.6M reaction dataset and fine-tuned it with ChemCensor-based and novelty rewards for retrosynthesis.
key_points: Introduces Top-K prompting as a training and inference paradigm to capture diverse, chemically plausible retrosynthetic reactions.
Compiles CREED-CCV-2+USPTO-XL, an ultra-large-scale dataset containing approximately 45.6 million verified chemical reactions.
Trains Chemistry Constraint-Consistent Language Model (C3LM) using fine-tuning integrated with ChemCensor-based and novelty-oriented rewards.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on the out-of-distribution URSA-expert-2026 benchmark.
Demonstrates that LLMs and conventional models explore complementary reaction spaces, supporting ensemble retrosynthesis systems.
summary.why_it_matters: Plausibility-aware Top-K training enables LLMs to generate more diverse and valid reaction pathways, advancing computer-aided synthesis planning.

papers.title: MoE-ViE: Mixture of Experts Vision Encoder for Efficient Image and Video Understanding

summary.tldr: MoE-ViE applies fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts, auxiliary-loss-free balancing, custom inference kernels, and frame-level distillation to scale CLIP-style vision encoders efficiently for image and video understanding.
key_points: Fine-grained MoE topologies and an auxiliary-loss-free expert balancing mechanism improve expert utilization over standard MoE designs.
Frame-level distillation combined with a novel freezing mechanism enhances video processing capabilities while maintaining base image knowledge.
A specialized MoE kernel mitigates routing and execution latency overhead during inference.
The largest MoE-ViE model matches zero-shot performance of a SOTA dense encoder 1.7x its size at 76% of the latency.
When integrated into a vision-language model, MoE-ViE outperforms baseline encoders on image and video benchmarks, including models with up to 5x more activated parameters.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that MoE vision encoders can achieve state-of-the-art vision-language multimodal performance while significantly reducing compute costs and inference latency compared to dense architectures.

papers.title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated looped language models on compositional tool calling, finding that recurrent computation at inference time significantly improves multi-step tool coordination, state maintenance, and dependency resolution.
key_points: Evaluated native and retrofitted looped language models against non-looped baselines using API-Bank, BFCL, and NESTful benchmarks under matched supervised fine-tuning recipes.
Recurrent computation provided consistent gains on compositional and dependency-aware tool workflows, while yielding smaller, model-dependent improvements on single isolated API calls.
Multi-step tool invocation accuracy scaled directly with recurrent depth at inference time.
Adaptive inference strategies optimized the compute-performance trade-off by dynamically routing additional recurrent compute steps only to complex tool interactions.
summary.why_it_matters: Looped architectures allow agentic AI systems to execute complex multi-step tool workflows more reliably by dynamically allocating compute during inference without increasing parameter count.

papers.title: Decision-Metric Alignment in Latent World Models: Diagnostics and Action-Conditioned Objectives for MPC Planning

summary.tldr: This paper introduces diagnostics and an action-conditioned objective, DA-LeWM, to fix decision-metric misalignment where latent distance fails to correctly rank action sequences in MPC planning.
key_points: Identifies 'decision-metric alignment' as the degree to which Euclidean distance in JEPA-style latent space correctly ranks action sequences by actual task progress.
Introduces two diagnostic metrics, Plan-Real Spearman and CEM-stage Spearman, to measure rank agreement between latent and real costs across random plans and concentrating CEM proposal distributions.
Identifies encoder distortion, terminal rollout error, and candidate margins as the primary mathematical drivers controlling rank preservation.

Proposes DA-LeWM, which adds inverse-dynamics and demonstration-conditioned goal-action heads to LeWM to improve latent geometry for CEM-based MPC, achieving faster convergence and higher task success without altering probe scores.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that strong latent decoding performance is insufficient for planning, proving that explicitly optimizing latent geometry for decision alignment significantly improves online MPC success.

papers.title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation

summary.tldr: SoftVTBench introduces a dataset of 4,000 expert visuo-tactile demonstrations with FEM ground-truth and a benchmark evaluating deformable-object manipulation via a novel Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR).
key_points: Dataset provides 4,000 expert demonstrations across >50 assets (volumetric deformable objects and rigid twins) synchronized at 20 Hz with multi-view RGB, dual-finger tactile data, proprioception, and evaluator-only FEM states.
Defines the Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR), which requires both task completion and maintaining peak normalized object deformation within a calibrated tolerance.
Benchmarking Diffusion Policy, π_{0.5}, and FastWAM showed 0.7–24% of successful in-distribution task rollouts violated safety deformation limits.
Visuo-tactile variants improved task success in all 6 out-of-distribution tests and improved DSR in 5, though in-distribution gains were mixed.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes that standard task-completion metrics overlook physical damage during manipulation, providing a standardized framework to develop safer multimodal policies.

papers.title: Harness Continual Learning: Continual Adaptation Beyond Model Parameters

summary.tldr: Harness Continual Learning (HCL) introduces a framework for evolving a frozen foundation model's external harness—including prompts, memories, tools, and routers—while mitigating harness-level catastrophic forgetting.
key_points: Formulates Harness Continual Learning (HCL) to adapt agent state outside of model parameters using four components: Task Interface, Experience Memory, Capability Map, and Adaptive Router.
Introduces guarded harness evolution, decoupling candidate update generation by a Continual Optimizer from state commitment by a Continual Evaluator.
Employs a Continual Evaluator that validates candidate harnesses against current task improvement, historical behavior retention, and overall validity before committing changes.

Demonstrates >10% relative gains over baselines in textual reasoning, multimodal perception, and open-world interaction tasks, while enabling explicit adjustment of the stability-plasticity trade-off.
summary.why_it_matters: HCL enables persistent agent improvement and failure recovery through external prompt and memory updates without expensive model fine-tuning or parameter degradation.

papers.title: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild: Why Exploitation, Not Exploration, Is the Bottleneck

summary.tldr: A compute-normalized comparison across five open-ended domains reveals that test-time scaling fails due to poor candidate exploitation rather than insufficient exploration.
key_points: Exploration scales effectively across all benchmarks, steadily improving the quality of the best candidate in the generated pool.
Exploitation fails because reward models correlate weakly (rho_v approximately 0.12) with true candidate quality on state-of-the-art generators.
Tree search exacerbates exploitation failures via diversity collapse, while iterative refinement only improves performance on one of five benchmarks.
Fusion (synthesis across candidates) is the only method that consistently outperforms single-sample baselines, though it captures only about 40% of available potential quality.
summary.why_it_matters: Increasing inference compute via current test-time scaling methods yields diminishing returns in open-ended domains unless reward models and candidate selection mechanisms are substantially improved.

papers.title: Training-Free Inference-Time Self-Reflection and Cost-Bounded Early Stopping for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: EvoResearcher is a training-free inference protocol that implements cost-bounded self-reflection and early stopping on a frozen LLM backbone without gradient updates.
key_points: Executes an iterative generate-critique-revise loop up to a max depth D or until a CONFIRMED sentinel triggers early stopping.
Uses four prompt-level meta-reward mechanisms: correctness, efficiency, reflection depth, and tool-call diversity.
Evaluated on Big-Bench Hard (100 items), GSM8K (500), and MATH (500) using Qwen2.5-72B for cross-model replication.
Early stopping terminates 82-88% of items early, averaging ~2.1 generations per question while maintaining baseline accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLMs to self-verify and optimize compute budgets at inference time without requiring costly reinforcement learning pipelines like GRPO.

papers.title: Learned, Then Lost: A Measured Single-Example Counterfactual in Pre-training

summary.tldr: Researchers measured the exact counterfactual impact of a single 194-token training injection across 32 124M-parameter GPT-2 models, finding the memory rapidly decays and leaves no detectable final trace on loss barriers or CKA.
key_points: Tested 32 GPT-2 124M models across four injection conditions (real passage, gradient-matched fabricated passage, random characters, and uninjected control) at step 200 of 9,536.
The single-exposure passage was initially learned, showing a statistically significant 0.039 to 0.044 nats cross-entropy improvement 50 steps post-injection across 8 seeds (p < 10^-4).
By the final step, the loss difference decayed below statistical detection (p = 0.25 and p = 0.71), and CKA failed to separate conditions at any layer.

Weight displacement reached 44.1% of seed-to-seed Euclidean distance (92% settled by mid-training), whereas interpolation loss barrier reached only 3.0% of the seed-to-seed barrier, confirming the model shifted basins without leaving it.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that single-example pre-training memory rapidly decays without altering final loss basins provides empirical grounding for counterfactual data attribution and privacy limits in large language models.

papers.title: Gradient Mirage: Trainable yet Label-Unidentifiable Gradients in Large Language Model Split Learning

summary.tldr: Gradient Mirage defends LLM split learning against gradient matching attacks by disrupting gradient-objective consistency while preserving model utility.
key_points: Breaks gradient-objective consistency across three dimensions: objective (Selective Autoregressive Supervision via a masked surrogate loss), scale (Scale Blinding via randomized multiplicative rescaling), and direction (Directional Privatization via the von Mises-Fisher mechanism).
Forces adversaries to solve a misspecified inverse problem where no plausible label sequence in the sequence space can explain the exposed gradients.
Preserves model utility using Dual-Track Backpropagation to train the Top segment on all target tokens and Bottom-Gradient Recovery to restore effective gradients for the Bottom segment.
Provides a stronger privacy-utility trade-off and superior protection compared to existing defenses under equivalent fine-tuning performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables secure split learning of large language models by preventing malicious servers from recovering private training labels from shared interface gradients.

papers.title: WhiteMatter: All-to-All Cross-Layer Connections via KV Mixing

summary.tldr: WhiteMatter introduces all-to-all cross-layer connections that route and mix a token's L layer states into k KV-cache channels for subsequent consumer layers to attend to.
key_points: A token-level router mixes L layer representations into k cached KV channels, allowing consumer layers to attend to representations from different depths of past tokens.
Connection weights vary across consumer layers and dynamically adapt based on the source token.
Setting the channel count k < L compresses the KV-cache memory footprint.
In pretraining experiments, WhiteMatter outperformed a vanilla Transformer with 50% more layers and maintained most gains under 50% KV-cache compression.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves Transformer parameter efficiency and performance while significantly reducing KV-cache memory overhead during decoding.

papers.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments

summary.tldr: SPADE is a self-play RL framework where a single LLM acts as both an Environment Designer generating executable code environments and a Reasoning Agent learning to solve them.
key_points: The Environment Designer writes complete, long-horizon environments featuring state transitions, reward functions, and verification code via an OpenAI Gym-style reset()/step() interface.
Targeted, feasible environment generation is guided by optimizing a regret signal derived from the gap between the Reasoning Agent's reward with and without privileged hints.
Critical designer components include grounding on pretraining corpus documents and utilizing an accumulated environment memory.
Scaling to 30B-parameter models yields an average +5.3 improvement across eight math, science, code, and reasoning benchmarks over the strongest fixed-environment baseline.
Tool-use performance increases by +5.7 on BFCL-v4 multi-turn and +13.9 on ACEBench-Agent, with performance margins widening as model scale grows.
summary.why_it_matters: By making environment synthesis learnable and adaptive rather than static, SPADE enables continuous open-ended self-improvement for language models across complex reasoning and tool-use tasks.

papers.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning

summary.tldr: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation (GC-OPD) resolves teacher-verifier misalignment in long-context reasoning by combining group-normalized trajectory residuals with token-level Relative-Advantage-Based Credit Assignment (RACA).
key_points: Identifies that token-level teacher scores in standard On-Policy Distillation (OPD) misalign with trajectory-level verifier rewards as input context lengths scale.
Calculates a signed teacher-verifier disagreement residual by separately normalizing verifier rewards and OPD trajectory scores within each rollout group.
Applies Relative-Advantage-Based Credit Assignment (RACA) to distribute trajectory-level residuals across tokens proportionally to their relative OPD advantages rather than uniformly.
Improves 5-benchmark long-context averages for Qwen3-4B (29.08 to 40.47) and Qwen3-8B (35.12 to 44.65), outperforming vanilla OPD baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-context language models to retain dense token-level training guidance from teacher models while ensuring alignment with global, response-level task verifiers.

papers.title: Beyond the Transcript: Detecting Covert Co ordination in Latent Multi-Agent Communication

summary.tldr: Verifiable Latent Alignments (VLA) is a framework that monitors and mitigates covert language-model multi-agent communication in continuous hidden states using an activation-aware, neutral-only three-layer monitor and matched counterfactual steering.
key_points: VLA links private latent-state records to public actions via shared event identifiers for matched causal analysis across black-box instructions and white-box counterfactuals.

The sequential monitor combines representation anomaly detection, counterfactual action-distribution influence, and sparse-autoencoder interpretation without training the primary monitor on attack examples.
The monitor achieved a mean AUROC of 0.993 for homogeneous agent pairs and 0.854 for heterogeneous pairs when pooling text- and latent-collusion positives.

In Qwen3-0.6B auctions with 25-100 bidders, full white-box steering achieved 100% bid-distribution recovery by replaying matched neutral counterfactuals and reduced collusive low-bid behavior by 47.3 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that covert, non-transcript multi-agent collusion via continuous hidden states can be effectively detected and steered back to neutral behavior without prior training on attack patterns.

papers.title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Open-MOPD diagnoses capability integration failures in multi-teacher on-policy distillation and introduces three budget-rebalancing mechanisms, improving headroom recovery from 35.6% to 83.4% on SmolLM3-3B-Base.
key_points: Identifies that standard M-OPD captures only 35.6% of headroom due to token-level optimization budget misallocation rather than gradient conflict.
Isolates three causes of failure: sequence-length disparities, dynamic convergence drift from non-uniform learning rates, and reward staleness from asynchronous updates.
Introduces token-share balancing, gap-aware dynamic budget allocation, and student reward refresh to correct cross-domain imbalances.
Provides an open-source, fully reproducible end-to-end post-training recipe designed for an academically accessible hardware budget.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the effective consolidation of multiple domain-specialized RL expert models into a single generalist student without suffering severe cross-domain performance degradation.

security.title: Catastrophic Learning: A New Attack Vector on Continual Learning Networks

summary.tldr: Researchers identified a novel Continual Learning attack vector called catastrophic learning, where adversarial learning blockers target network plasticity to impede future task acquisition while simultaneously triggering catastrophic forgetting.
key_points: Introduces learning blockers, an adversarial data manipulation that targets algorithm plasticity to reduce learnability of current or future unseen iterations.
Proposes six specific attack strategies: Label-Exchange, Tensor-Exchange, Attraction-Coincident, Attraction-Preceding, Repulsion-Coincident, and Repulsion-Preceding.

Attraction variants pull feature space representations together by minimizing loss between poisoned and victim iteration labels, while Repulsion variants maximize this loss so stability mechanisms resist parameter shifts.
Evaluated across more than 4,480 simulations on MNIST and Split-CIFAR10 against three standard Continual Learning defense strategies: DER, ER-ACE, and iCaRL.
summary.why_it_matters: This attack vector exposes a critical security flaw in continual learning models where attackers can silently compromise a model's ability to learn future data streams before those data streams are even encountered.

security.title: FedLNS: Leverage LayerNorm Signature Modeling to Mitigate Adversarial Manipulation in Federated LLMs

summary.tldr: FedLNS is a server-side framework that detects malicious updates in federated LLMs by modeling changes in LayerNorm parameters against a robust, history-aware reference without requiring extra client metadata or raw data.
key_points: Extracts client signatures purely from returned model weights by tracking changes in trainable normalization-layer (LayerNorm) parameters.
Operates entirely on the server side without needing trusted datasets, labeled attack examples, auxiliary detectors, or added communication overhead.
Screens and filters out suspicious updates prior to standard or robust federated aggregation.
Evaluated on GPT, BERT, and LLaMA architectures with 200 clients, achieving lower test perplexity than six baselines under 40% target manipulation across both IID and non-IID data distributions.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables federated LLM training to withstand heavy data manipulation attacks without compromising client privacy or requiring additional network bandwidth.

security.title: Task-Conditioned Least-Privilege Learning for Executable Terminal and MCP Agents

summary.tldr: A post-training framework trains a 4B parameter model to minimize excess authority by auditing task actions against deterministic verifiers and task-specific authority envelopes.
key_points: Evaluates agent actions pre-execution and post-effect using deterministic verifiers across six risk dimensions (completion, evidence, exact state, prohibited attempts, and safe success).
Post-training Qwen3.5-4B over 1,500 tasks increased safe success from 64.36% to 98.48% across 2,896 evaluation episodes.
Reduces excess-authority error events from 4.56% to 0.79% in main evaluations, and by 6.99 percentage points in a 400-task continuation study without losing capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: Learned restraint via post-training provides a effective defense-in-depth layer to prevent excess-privilege actions in terminal and Model Context Protocol (MCP) environments, though traditional permission gating and sandboxing remain necessary.

security.title: MemCatalyst: Amplifying Data Auditing on Vision-Language Models via Data Poisoning

summary.tldr: MemCatalyst uses Poisoning Text and Poisoning Image strategies to force Vision-Language Models to over-learn image-text inconsistencies, significantly enhancing membership inference data auditing performance with a minimal sample budget.
key_points: Introduces MemCatalyst, a data poisoning framework comprising Poisoning Text (PT) and Poisoning Image (PI) strategies.
Forces VLMs to memorize specific inconsistencies between textual semantics and image features during training to amplify membership information leakage.
Demonstrates effective transferability of poisoned samples across different VLM architectures in black-box auditing scenarios.
Validated against five state-of-the-art data auditing techniques on two prominent VLMs, increasing MI AUC scores while maintaining negligible impact on model utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables content creators and data holders to reliably detect unauthorized use of their intellectual property in Vision-Language Model training sets without degrading model performance.

security.title: Improving LLM-Based SSH Honeypots Through Prompting and Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated prompt design and supervised fine-tuning across eight models to improve shell emulation realism in local open-weight LLM-based SSH honeypots.
key_points: Local open-weight LLMs prevent cost exploitation, provider changes, and versioning issues seen in cloud models, but suffer from command echoing, malformed outputs, and inconsistent filesystem states.
Evaluation used 34 automated unit tests assessing single-session and fresh-session shell emulation accuracy across seven local open-weight models and a fine-tuned GPT-3.5 model.

Fine-tuning performance depended strictly on dataset coverage: the original 112-conversation dataset yielded no aggregate pass rate improvement, whereas an expanded dataset derived from real honeypot logs significantly improved local models.
Combining strong rule-based prompt engineering with supervised fine-tuning showed conflicting interactions due to redundant enforcement of shell-behavior constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that local open-weight LLMs can effectively emulate SSH shells without cloud dependencies if fine-tuned on real honeypot log datasets and properly prompted.

security.title: CTIFoundry: An Agent-Native Corpus Scaffold for Cyber Threat Intelligence

summary.tldr: CTIFoundry is an agent-native corpus scaffold that transforms unstructured threat intelligence into a deterministic ontology graph and typed tool surface, significantly improving agentic investigation performance.
key_points: Materializes a deterministic ontology graph using official cross-references across CVE, CWE, CAPEC, and ATT&CK as typed, traversable edges.
Features a span-grounded report layer with canonical, alias-resolved cross-vendor entities indexing provenance-carrying chunks and hybrid dense+lexical retrieval.
Exposes the corpus structure at query time via seven typed tools and three procedural skills on a standard open-source agent harness.
Improves overall F1 score by +0.19 to +0.28 on the CTIConnect benchmark across four models, enabling smaller models to outperform flagship models on flat substrates.
Reduces tool call volume by approximately half on Claude models while increasing accuracy, with ablations showing super-additive composition between typed structure and procedural skills.
summary.why_it_matters: Replacing flat vector databases with structured, agent-native corpora allows LLM security agents to conduct faster, more accurate threat investigations using fewer compute resources.

security.title: Denoising-Aware Inversion: Revealing Privacy Risks in Noise-Protected Text Embeddings

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced DAEI, a denoising-aware embedding inversion pipeline using a residual autoencoder and Stein's unbiased risk estimate, breaking standard Gaussian noise defenses on text embeddings.
key_points: Identifies the Double Noise Trap that causes standard generative embedding inversion models to fail on perturbed outputs.
Introduces DAEI, combining a residual denoising autoencoder with generative text inversion to reconstruct text without clean target access.
Trains the denoiser in an unsupervised manner using Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimate (SURE) on noisy observations alone.
Achieves a ~154% relative BLEU improvement and a 32-60% increase in token-level F1 and ROUGE-L over generative baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that adding Gaussian noise to text embeddings is insufficient to prevent sensitive privacy leakage against adaptive attackers.

security.title: Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter

summary.tldr: OpenAI has introduced Privacy Filter, a 1.5B parameter bidirectional token-classification model designed to detect and redact PII and secrets in text using a single forward pass.
key_points: Derived from an autoregressively pretrained checkpoint and converted into a bidirectional, banded-attention classifier with 50M active parameters per token.
Employs a constrained Viterbi decoder to output coherent spans across eight distinct privacy categories.
Supports a 128,000-token context window and provides configurable operating points for precision-recall tradeoffs during local deployment.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient, local, high-context data minimization within layered privacy workflows without relying on external APIs.

security.title: Redakto - The Incognito Tab for LLMs

summary.tldr: Redakto is an open-source, locally deployable tool providing PII redaction and pseudonymization for LLM inputs via a web app, REST APIs, and MCP hooks without significantly impacting task utility.
key_points: Provides state-of-the-art PII redaction and pseudonymization capabilities designed to sanitize text prior to downstream LLM processing.
Exposes interfaces for end-users via a web application and for developers/researchers through REST APIs and Model Context Protocol (MCP) hooks.
Fully open source and optimized for low compute requirements to support local hardware deployment.
Evaluated empirically on legal and medical domain texts, demonstrating that redacted output maintains utility scores on par with original unredacted texts.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables privacy-compliant LLM integration and compliance with EU data regulations without sacrificing downstream task performance or exposing sensitive PII to external models.

security.title: FESC: Remodeling Long-Context Private Inference with Encrypted State-Space Models

summary.tldr: FESC is a hybrid FHE-MPC system for private long-context selective State-Space Model (SSM) inference that achieves linear-time performance without quadratic Transformer bottlenecks.
key_points: Uses a factorized scan-contract algorithm to stream state chunks on demand, compress input-dependent transitions, and prevent dense FHE-MPC conversions.
Combines GPU-optimized CKKS encryption kernels for linear operations with MPC protocols for non-linear functions including SiLU, softplus, exponential, and RMSNorm.
Employs approximation-aware fine-tuning to preserve near-plaintext model accuracy.
Executes a 12-layer Mamba-base model at sequence length L=2,048 on a single A100 GPU in 77.3 minutes with a 32.7 GB peak memory footprint.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables private end-to-end processing of long-context documents using linear-time SSM architectures like Mamba-2 on single-GPU infrastructure.

security.title: Geometric Data Perturbation with Noisy-Anchor Alignment for Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Learning

summary.tldr: A novel Geometric Data Perturbation scheme perturbs shared anchor representations rather than private-data representations to maintain downstream model accuracy while preventing data recovery under analyst-participant collusion.
key_points: Analyst-participant collusion can compromise non-colluding private data when using shared-anchor alignment from Data Collaboration (DC).
Adding noise directly to private-data representations mitigates leakage but degrades utility, whereas adding noise to anchor representations preserves a better privacy-utility trade-off.
Participants independently transform private data and a shared anchor matrix, perturbing only the anchor representation before a single-round upload.
The central analyst uses the noisy anchor representations to align private-data representations by solving a Generalized Orthogonal Procrustes Problem.
Empirical validation on MNIST and CelebA demonstrates higher learning accuracy than private-data noise under equivalent measured leakage.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate one-shot collaborative learning across multiple parties without exposing private raw data to colluding participants and analysts.

security.title: Diff-DDoS: Realistic Cyber-Physical Attack Synthesis and Robust Detection for 5G-Enabled CPS Using Tabular Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: Diff-DDoS uses a tabular denoising diffusion probabilistic model (TabDDPM) with inverse classifier guidance to generate distribution-preserving DDoS attacks and harden 5G cyber-physical intrusion detectors via adversarial training.
key_points: Baseline detectors trained on hand-crafted attacks suffer severe performance degradation, with F1-score drops ranging from 47% to 100% when exposed to realistic attacks.

The three-phase Diff-DDoS framework trains a baseline CNN detector on CDR spatiotemporal grids, synthesizes realistic attacks using TabDDPM, and iteratively hardens models via Adversarial Diffusion Training (ADT).
Evaluated on a Milano CDR dataset, ADT paired with ResNet50 recovers F1-scores to 79.62% for silent-call, 100% for Internet-signaling, and 92.79% for blended attack scenarios.

Following validation-based threshold calibration, ADT achieves a 100% F1-score on SMS-flooding, outperforming CTGAN (47.3%) and matching top gradient-based adversarial training baselines on silent-call attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that tabular diffusion models can effectively synthesize realistic attack traffic to stress-test and defensively harden intrusion detection systems in data-scarce 5G deployments.

security.title: The Last Mile of Deepfake Speech Detection: An Industry-Academia Experience Report

summary.tldr: A three-year industry-academia collaboration with Phonexia identifies critical barriers in deploying deepfake speech detection, including restrictive dataset licensing, benchmark audio mismatches, and uninterpretable log-likelihood ratio scores.
key_points: Commercial deployment faces licensing restrictions on public benchmarks, limiting their use in model development.
Real-world inputs deviate from public benchmarks, consisting of long, codec-degraded, and partially synthetic recordings rather than short, clean clips.
Calibrated system outputs, such as a log-likelihood ratio of 2.5, lack actionable interpretability for non-expert customers.
The authors advocate for commercially usable datasets, realistic deployment benchmarks, and standardized, interpretable scoring.
summary.why_it_matters: Solving these deployment barriers is necessary to translate near-perfect academic deepfake detection metrics into reliable, real-world commercial security systems.

infra.title: Building Federated Multimodal AI Workflows with NVIDIA FLARE

summary.tldr: NVIDIA FLARE enables federated learning workflows for vision-language models across distributed institutions without centralizing raw data.
key_points: Supports distributed adaptation of vision-language models (VLMs) for visual question answering, captioning, and image-text reasoning.
Coordinates collaborative AI training across multiple data-local sites while keeping raw records decentralized.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows organizations to train advanced multimodal models on private or geographically restricted datasets without violating data privacy or governance rules.

infra.title: Post-Train NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge for On-Device Robot Control

summary.tldr: NVIDIA introduced Cosmos 3 Edge, a 4B omni-world model designed for on-device robot control.
key_points: Cosmos 3 Edge is a 4-billion parameter omni-model in the Cosmos 3 family.
It incorporates a 2-billion parameter NVIDIA Nemotron-based reasoner.
The model enables learning physical interactions while addressing on-device deployment constraints for onboard computing hardware.
summary.why_it_matters: It brings physical world model foundation capabilities directly to onboard robotic hardware by addressing model size limitations.

infra.title: Asynchronous patterns for calling Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents in serverless pipelines

summary.tldr: AWS details asynchronous invocation patterns for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents in serverless Step Functions pipelines to eliminate idle compute costs caused by synchronous blocking callers.
key_points: Synchronous calls to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents force calling compute services like AWS Lambda to remain active and incur full runtime costs while waiting for responses.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime uses a consumption-based model that does not charge for CPU while the agent is idling on LLM responses or Model Context Protocol (MCP) calls.
The article evaluates three non-blocking asynchronous architectural patterns—task-token callback, direct service integration, and durable functions—against the synchronous blocking anti-pattern.
The demonstration uses a five-stage real-estate document processing pipeline (Extract, Identify, Route, Organize and Validate, Result) where only the agent invocation branch is modified.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling caller compute execution from agent reasoning time prevents substantial AWS Lambda billing waste during long-running generative AI agent workflows.

vendors.title: Offering Zero Data Retention for frontier models

summary.tldr: OpenAI has reaffirmed Zero Data Retention for eligible API customers and previewed Private Safety Processing to maintain advanced AI safety alongside data privacy.
key_points: Reaffirms Zero Data Retention (ZDR) availability for eligible API customers.
Previews Private Safety Processing to execute AI safety checks without compromising customer data privacy.
summary.why_it_matters: API customers can process sensitive data through frontier models with guaranteed zero data retention while maintaining safety standards.

vendors.title: Replit expands access to software creation with GPT-5.6 Luna

summary.tldr: Replit has introduced Free Mode powered by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna, allowing users to build software without token costs.
key_points: Replit is launching Free Mode for software creation.
The new feature is powered by the GPT-5.6 Luna model.
Free Mode eliminates token cost concerns for users building applications.
summary.why_it_matters: Removing token cost barriers allows developers and non-technical users to build and iterate on software using advanced AI models for free.

vendors.title: LFM2.5 Q4\_0 Checkpoints from Quantization-Aware Distillation

summary.tldr: Liquid AI has released LFM2.5 Q4_0 checkpoints created using quantization-aware distillation to optimize model compression.
key_points: Releases Q4_0 quantized checkpoints for the LFM2.5 model series on Hugging Face.
Utilizes quantization-aware distillation (QAD) to preserve model accuracy at lower bit-widths.
summary.why_it_matters: Quantization-aware distillation provides higher-fidelity 4-bit quantized models, reducing memory usage and computational overhead without severe performance degradation.

vendors.title: smolmachines / smolvm as a sandbox for untrusted Python & JavaScript

summary.tldr: Claude Fable 5 bypassed the lack of nested virtualization in Claude Code for web by executing smolvm sandbox evaluation tests within a GitHub Actions runner exposing /dev/kvm.
key_points: Claude Code for web runs inside a Firecracker guest (Linux 6.18.5-fc-v20) lacking /dev/kvm and vmx/svm CPU flags, preventing smolvm execution.
The agent targeted smolmachines/smolvm as a fast, secure sandbox for untrusted Python and JavaScript execution with strict RAM, CPU, network, and filesystem constraints.
To overcome the lack of nested virtualization, the agent autonomously created a temporary GitHub Actions workflow on Ubuntu runners, which expose /dev/kvm, to complete the test suite.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that advanced coding agents can dynamically re-route hardware-dependent testing tasks to external CI/CD environments when local containers lack required KVM privileges.

summary.tldr: Jeremy Morrell hypothesizes a new opportunity for web-based extensible software driven by LLM-assisted extension authoring and modern sandbox primitives.
key_points: LLMs radically lower the authoring cost of application extensions.
Modern sandbox primitives lower deployment costs while providing secure execution boundaries.
Architectural approach relies on a solid, accountable core combined with LLM-generated extensions to fill functional gaps.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining secure sandboxing with low-cost LLM code generation allows applications to provide safe, user-driven software extensibility.
